skill.name: image-inpainting
skill.description: Guides mask-driven image inpainting with the RunComfy CLI. It helps choose Z-Image Turbo Inpainting for masked edits and description-based edit models when no mask is available.
skill.summary: Run precise RunComfy image inpainting with masks, prompts, strength, and model routing guidance.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, covert data exfiltration, or malicious filesystem behavior was found in the reviewed skill file. The static findings are false positives from Markdown code formatting, documented RunComfy URLs, sample CLI usage, and normal token storage documentation. The main residual consideration is expected privacy exposure because user-provided image and mask URLs are sent to RunComfy services.

remediation.suggestion: Keep the documentation explicit that images, masks, prompts, and output requests are processed by RunComfy services.
Continue separating CLI installation guidance from agent-executed actions, and keep agent bash scope limited to RunComfy commands.
Maintain the documented token file permissions and recommend environment variables for CI or container use.

content.value_statement: Mask-driven image edits can be slow when prompts, masks, and model choices are handled manually. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to run RunComfy inpainting with the right model and inputs.
actual_capabilities: Routes masked edits to Z-Image Turbo Inpainting through the RunComfy CLI.
Builds inpainting inputs with image URL, mask URL, prompt, strength, and control scale.
Suggests description-based edit models when no usable mask is available.
Provides guidance for object removal, background replacement, blemish cleanup, and region replacement.
Explains RunComfy CLI setup, authentication, output directories, and common exit codes.
limitations: Requires an installed RunComfy CLI and authenticated RunComfy access.
Needs source image and mask URLs for precise inpainting.
Does not create masks, extend canvases, or edit video frames.
Sends user-provided image and mask URLs to RunComfy services.

use_cases.title: Clean Product Backgrounds
use_cases.description: Replace masked product backgrounds with consistent studio surfaces while preserving the product edges.

use_cases.title: Retouch Local Image Defects
use_cases.description: Remove small distractions, blemishes, or damaged areas from user-owned images with controlled masks.

use_cases.title: Apply Styled Region Replacements
use_cases.description: Use LoRA-capable inpainting routes when a masked area must match a brand or visual style.

prompt_templates.title: Remove a Masked Object
prompt_templates.prompt: Inpaint the masked area in [image URL] using [mask URL]. Remove [object] and preserve [areas to keep].

prompt_templates.title: Replace a Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace the masked background in [image URL] with [new background]. Keep the subject unchanged and blend the mask edge naturally.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Cleanup Strength
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RunComfy inpainting for [image URL] and [mask URL]. Set strength near 0.5 for cleanup and keep nearby textures matched.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Best Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best RunComfy route for this edit. I have [mask or no mask], [image URL], and need [goal], while preserving [constraints].

output_examples.input: A product photo has a mask over a cluttered background.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo Inpainting, fills the masked background with clean studio paper, and saves the result to the output directory.

output_examples.input: A street photo has masked overhead cables.
output_examples.output: The skill removes the cables, asks RunComfy to preserve rooflines and sky gradients, and reports where the edited image was downloaded.

output_examples.input: A user describes a local edit but has no mask image.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a description-based edit model and frames the prompt to preserve everything outside the requested region.

best_practices: Use masks that match the source image dimensions and align with the intended edit region.
State what must remain unchanged outside the mask.
Confirm permission before removing watermarks, logos, or identifying marks.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse a mask from a different source image.
Do not send private or regulated images to external services without approval.
Do not use high strength values for subtle cleanup unless full replacement is intended.

faq.question: Does this skill create masks?
faq.answer: No. It consumes image and mask URLs. Create masks with an image editor or segmentation tool first.

faq.question: Which model does it use for masked edits?
faq.answer: It defaults to Tongyi MAI Z-Image Turbo Inpainting when a mask is available.

faq.question: What happens when I do not have a mask?
faq.answer: The skill recommends description-based edit models such as Nano Banana 2 Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, or FLUX Kontext Pro.

faq.question: Can it remove watermarks?
faq.answer: It can guide watermark cleanup, but only use it when you own the content or have permission.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: RunComfy downloads completed results into the output directory selected for the CLI run.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No. The RunComfy CLI sends the request to RunComfy model services and downloads the result.
